transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-22 14:30 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Northshore - Head of Security), Liam O'Connell (Platform Engineer), Aisha Mensah (Compliance), Jon Park (Infra)

Summary:
Short kickoff to align on what admin/activity is captured by Redwood, how exports work (S3/syslog/Kafka), KMS/encryption considerations, and retention/legal hold needs for Northshore Trust. Walkthrough of a proposed evidence handoff playbook and next steps for a 1-week export pilot to Northshore's Splunk environment.

Topics: audit capture; admin actions vs. user content; export destinations; retention windows; encryption at rest/in transit; KMS key ownership and rotation; legal hold; demo of export UI and sample payloads.

00:00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Quick round robin?
00:00:06 Priya: Priya here, head of security. We're responsible for audit compliance and e-discovery at Northshore.
00:00:10 Liam: Liam, platform, I'll be doing the integration work.
00:00:13 Aisha: Aisha, compliance lead, I'll own retention policy questions.
00:00:17 Jon: Jon, infra, here for the S3/network stuff.
00:00:20 Maya: Great, Diego from our SE team will lead the technical bits. Diego?
00:00:24 Diego: Hi all. Goal for today is to clarify what events we capture, how to route them to your systems, options for KMS, and any legal hold patterns you need. Also want to show a short export demo.

00:01:12 Priya: To start, high level — are admin events complete? We need to see role changes, policy changes, API key issuance, logins, failed logins, SSO events, integration webhooks, user deletes, that sort of thing. Do you capture every admin API call?
00:01:28 Diego: Yes, we capture admin actions across the console and API. There's a slight nuance — we capture the intented action and metadata: actor, ip, timestamp, service, before/after snapshot when available. Occasionally delta snapshots are summarized for heavy events, so you might see diffs for some bulk ops.
00:01:49 Priya: Ok, diffs are fine as long as we can reconstruct. Do you keep the full before/after by default?
00:01:55 Diego: Default retention in-hosted is 90 days full fidelity. For customers on Dedicated/Private we can enable extended retention or export real time to your collector for long-term storage.

00:02:20 Aisha: And what about content-level capture — do you capture user prompt/response payloads in these admin logs? We have PII concerns.
00:02:29 Diego: Admin logs do not include the raw model input/output by default. We capture admin-level metadata about model versions, model changes, and who triggered inferences but not the inference payload unless you opt into request-level logging. For regulated customers we recommend request masking or configure selective capture and route those to an encrypted bucket with restricted access.

00:03:06 Jon: For export destinations we have a Splunk cluster, and we also have an on-prem Kafka cluster. What options do you support?
00:03:14 Diego: We support direct S3 exports (parquet/ndjson rolling files), syslog forwarding, and Kafka producers to your cluster (TLS mutual auth). We also have a streaming webhook option for lightweight ingestion. For Splunk specifically, many customers ingest from S3 or via our syslog-to-splunk connector.

00:03:40 Priya: Encryption — who manages the KMS keys? We need Northshore to retain control where possible.
00:03:46 Diego: Two patterns: managed keys (Redwood KMS) for hosted customers, or customer-managed keys (CMK) in your AWS account using cross-account KMS grants for S3 exports and envelope encryption. For Dedicated/Private deployments we recommend CMKs or on-prem HSM -> Redwood will respect your key rotation and we can rotate wrapped keys.

00:04:08 Aisha: If we request legal hold for specific users, can you snapshot historical admin events beyond retention?
00:04:15 Diego: We can run forensics snapshots on demand — create an evidence package that packages events for a time window and persists it outside the default retention. That usually requires an HLD and often moves data to a locked S3 bucket with immutability. There's a cost delta.

00:04:40 Priya: Can that evidence package include sequence numbers and cryptographic hashes for chain of custody?
00:04:45 Diego: Yes, we can include checksums and a manifest. We also provide signing options when using customer HSM for signing.

00:05:05 Liam: On the export cadence — can we do near-real-time and also daily batches?
00:05:11 Diego: Yes, realtime streaming to Kafka or webhook. S3 batch placement windows are configurable — typically 5–15 minute slices, or you can do hourly/daily. For low-latency security alerts we'd recommend Kafka/syslog.

00:05:43 Jon: Network posture — your syslog endpoint — do we need to whitelist IP ranges or do you support VPC peering?
00:05:50 Diego: For hosted we provide a set of egress IP ranges to whitelist. For Private or Dedicated we support VPC peering and private endpoints so logs never traverse the public internet.

00:06:12 Priya: Data residency — we must keep audit exports in-country for EU customers. How do you guarantee region selection?
00:06:20 Maya: You can pin export buckets to specific cloud regions. For Private deployments we can keep the whole control plane in your region. For hosted we provide regional export endpoints and ensure data residency controls in our contract.

00:06:42 Aisha: How long can we keep admin logs? We have 7 years requirement for some records.
00:06:49 Diego: Default is 90 days. With exports to your storage you can keep indefinitely; for Dedicated we offer add-on long-retention tiers (1yr/3yr/7yr). We can also automate lifecycle rules to move data to cold storage (Glacier/Archive) after X days.

00:07:20 Priya: Ok, show us the demo for an S3 export and an evidence snapshot.
00:07:28 Diego: Sure. (a brief pause, mouseclicks) This is the export configuration UI; you pick source events (admin, auth, model-change, audit-config), format (ndjson/parquet), encryption options — use redwood-managed KMS or provide ARN for your CMK — and target. You can set batch window: 5m/15m/1h.
00:08:02 Diego: Example payload (ndjson) includes fields: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_email, actor_role, ip, action, target_resource, before_snapshot, after_snapshot, request_id, request_context. Note: long snapshots are truncated when delta compression is on; we include a full_snapshot flag when full_fidelity is enabled.

00:08:34 Priya: I see actor_role, but how does RBAC map between our enterprise SSO roles and Redwood's internal roles?
00:08:41 Diego: We support SAML/SCIM provisioning and role mapping. You can map your IdP groups to Redwood roles; we emit the mapped role in the actor_role field. If you need raw IdP attributes, we can include them in the export payload as extra fields behind a consent flag.

00:09:10 Aisha: For SSO login events — we need both SAML assertion details and IP/geo. Do you capture assertion IDs?
00:09:16 Diego: We capture assertion id and auth flow metadata, but not the full SAML XML for privacy. Assertion ID, saml_provider, success/failure, and failure reason are in the login event.

00:09:42 Jon: About regulatory e-discovery — we might need to tie an admin event back to model outputs. If you don't capture payloads by default, how do we reconcile?
00:09:51 Diego: You can enable request-level logging for a scoped set of teams or sessions. We recommend masking and redaction for PII. Another approach is to route request-level logs to a separate locked bucket with restricted IAM.

00:10:20 Priya: Are admin events tamper-evident? Could an operator with elevated privileges alter logs?
00:10:27 Diego: Good question. The control plane keeps an append-only event store; changes to logs require a second-level operation and are themselves logged (audit of audit). For stronger guarantees we can sign events on ingest and publish a daily digest signed by your CMK.

00:10:55 Aisha: Talk through retention + legal hold example: Suppose we need to hold all events for user X for 2 years.
00:11:03 Diego: We would tag events with legal-hold metadata and prevent lifecycle deletion for those objects, and optionally snapshot them into a write-once S3 bucket with object lock to meet compliance. We'll expose an API to place/remove holds.

00:11:30 Priya: We have a downstream SIEM – Splunk. For ingestion best practices, should we use S3 or syslog?
00:11:37 Diego: If you need historical replay capability S3 is simpler. For alerting you want syslog or Kafka for low latency. Most customers do both: S3 for cold storage/forensics, Kafka/syslog for real-time detection.

00:12:08 Liam: How granular are the event types? Can we get 'role-assignment' vs 'role-update' as separate action values?
00:12:15 Diego: Yes, action has a typed enum. We also include a human-readable action_description. You can subscribe to specific event types via the export filter.

00:12:42 Priya: About PII — if a prompt accidentally contains PII, and we have request logging enabled, how quickly can we purge on request?
00:12:50 Diego: We support targeted deletions using request_id; we can remove specific objects from the store and update manifests. For hosted customers we follow a documented process that includes legal verification. For private/dedicated customers you control the storage so you'd handle purges per your governance.

00:13:22 Maya: Quick note on SOC2/ISO: We'll send the SOC2 Type II report and our ISO scope doc. That should answer many of the audit/process questions.

00:13:33 Aisha: Great. One more detail — we require RBAC fine-grained for admin consoles. Can we extract an admin activity report scoped to particular RBAC roles?
00:13:43 Diego: Yep, query API supports filters by actor_role, actor_id, action, time range. We can produce CSV or JSON reports for those queries.

00:14:05 Priya: For the pilot, we want a 1-week export to our Splunk cluster, including admin and auth events, with CMK-managed encryption and hourly S3 batches plus syslog for alerts.
00:14:16 Liam: We'll want to test both batch replay and streaming. Also want sample event schemas to map to Splunk indexes.

00:14:28 Diego: I'll attach a schema doc and an example lifecycle policy. Also include a sample lambda for ingest to Splunk HEC from S3.

00:14:50 Maya: Ok let's capture explicit open questions so we can follow up.

00:15:00 Priya: 1) Can Redwood include assertion IDs and raw IdP attributes in export when requested? 2) Can evidence packages be immutable with object lock? 3) What is the cost estimate for 7-year retention?
00:15:15 Diego: We'll answer all three in the follow-up; cost depends on volume but we'll provide ballpark and sample calculation.

00:15:30 Jon: Technical nit — Kafka: do you support SASL/SCRAM or mTLS?
00:15:35 Diego: We support mTLS and SASL/SCRAM; we can fit into your existing Kafka security model.

00:16:00 Aisha: Compliance asks: how do you surface evidence for auditors? Do you provide a portal?
00:16:07 Maya: We provide an evidence export package and can do an auditor-only view via a signed, time-limited manifest. For enterprise customers we also support onsite evidence packages delivered to an agreed S3 bucket.

00:16:30 Priya: Any blockers for us?
00:16:33 Liam: We need the sample payloads and the runbook to estimate engineering work. Also we need a clear KMS integration blueprint.

00:16:45 Diego: Action items captured. I'll create the runbook, sample code, and a terraform snippet for S3 + KMS grant.

00:17:05 Maya: Couple of transcription quirks — sometimes speaker labels in your system come through as Speaker 1 etc. We will make sure exported events have proper actor identifiers mapped to your directory.

00:17:22 Priya: Anything else on legal hold?
00:17:25 Aisha: One ask — if an export is requested for legal discovery, include audit chain + signatures and a short manifest explaining transformations (e.g., truncation/deltas) so auditors understand.

00:17:40 Diego: Yes, manifest and md5/sha256 checksums included.

00:18:05 Maya: Ok last piece: we'll follow up with a proposed pilot plan. Any objections to the timeline?
00:18:12 Priya: No objections. We'll internally align and send retention matrix.

00:18:28 Maya: Great — end of recording.
